alphabet.title: Alphabet
alphabet.summary: US parent of Google; Android, Chrome and Google Search fall under the DMA rules on defaults and choice screens.

apple.title: Apple
apple.summary: US maker of iOS, iPadOS and Safari, which fall under the DMA rules on defaults and choice screens.

duck-duck-go.title: DuckDuckGo
duck-duck-go.summary: Company behind the DuckDuckGo search engine, which largely sources its web results from Bing.

ecosia.title: Ecosia
ecosia.summary: German search company that funds climate projects from ad revenue and co-owns the EUSP search index with Qwant.

european-search-perspective.title: European Search Perspective
european-search-perspective.summary: Paris-based joint venture of Ecosia and Qwant that runs the Staan European search index.

ionos.title: IONOS
ionos.summary: German hosting and cloud provider that runs IONOS Nextcloud Workspace in German data centres.

microsoft.title: Microsoft
microsoft.summary: US software and cloud vendor; Windows falls under the DMA rules on defaults, Bing and Edge do not.

mistral-ai.title: Mistral AI
mistral-ai.summary: French AI company behind the Vibe assistant (formerly Le Chat) and the Mistral models.

nextcloud.title: Nextcloud
nextcloud.summary: Stuttgart-based maker of the open-source Nextcloud collaboration platform, sold self-hosted or through hosting partners such as IONOS.

organic-maps.title: Organic Maps
organic-maps.summary: Estonian company behind the Organic Maps offline maps app, with a sole shareholder since August 2025.

proton.title: Proton
proton.summary: Swiss company behind Proton Mail, Proton Drive and Lumo, sold alone or in bundles.

qwant.title: Qwant
qwant.summary: Company behind the Qwant search engine; co-owns the EUSP search index with Ecosia and uses Microsoft for results it can't answer itself.

surfboard.title: Surfboard Holding B.V.
surfboard.summary: Dutch holding company that owns Startpage, listed as a subsidiary of the US company System1.

system1.title: System1
system1.summary: Publicly traded US company whose subsidiaries include Startpage's owner, Surfboard Holding B.V.

vivaldi-technologies.title: Vivaldi Technologies
vivaldi-technologies.summary: Norwegian browser maker behind Vivaldi, funded by search and bookmark partner deals.

court-of-justice-of-the-eu.title: Court of Justice of the European Union
court-of-justice-of-the-eu.summary: The EU's highest court. Its advocates general issue non-binding opinions that the court usually follows.

european-commission.title: European Commission
european-commission.summary: The EU's executive. Proposes EU laws such as the Digital Fairness Act and the Kids Act, and enforces the Digital Markets Act.

german-federal-government.title: German federal government
german-federal-government.summary: Germany's federal government under Chancellor Friedrich Merz. heise reports its intelligence services plan an offline cloud with Google as project partner.

digital-fairness-act.title: Digital Fairness Act
digital-fairness-act.summary: Planned EU law revamping online consumer protection. The Commission is due to propose it in November 2026.

digital-markets-act.title: Digital Markets Act
digital-markets-act.summary: EU competition law for large "gatekeeper" platforms, enforced by the European Commission. Covers defaults, choice screens, data portability and messaging interoperability.

kids-act.title: Kids Act
kids-act.summary: EU proposal from September 2026 to set common limits on social media access for minors, under negotiation.

cjeu-ai-press-publisher-case.title: Court of Justice case on AI chatbots and press publishers' rights
